response.text:
Make sure you know what you want to do as part of the induction. What do you not want to do today? How long do you want to spend doing this? (You don't have to do this on a problem. You can do it on something you want more of, like love or play or confidence, creativity, communion or whatever.) Make sure you allow some time at the end to come back and reflect on what you've experienced.

Make sure you're in a safe place to do this. Don't do it if you're driving a car or in the water or operating machinery or otherwise need to attend to yourself or others. If you're intoxicated or otherwise acutely confused or not able to keep yourself safe, get some support instead of doing exploratory hypnosis. If you're already partially or fully opened, see the section below on what to do if you're already open: contain yourself before you deepen.

Decide you're going to do it. How are you going to coax yourself to do this? Are you going to make it spacious? Warm and held? Whatever you want to do, but preview what you're going to do. Are you going to close your eyes? Are you going to come out and go back in again? What are you going to do at the end? If you're using a recording, read the script if you can. Remind yourself that if you say stop, you're going to stop this induction. If you say you want to do less, you'll be asked to do less. If you say quiet, the talking will stop. Or you can just open your eyes and come all the way back anyway. You don't have to ask your parts if it's okay to stop, even if they say you have to.
